text:
Situation: Lidocaine hydrochloride has been on the FDA drug shortage list since 2012-02-22 and remains current as of 2026-10-21. Multiple manufacturers are listed, including Amphastar, B. Braun, Baxter, Eugia, Fresenius Kabi, Hikma, and Hospira. Corvale Lakeside holds 3.9 to 4.2 days of supply across six lidocaine presentations. Corvale General holds approximately 6 days across six presentations. Corvale East holds 10.4 to 36.5 days across six presentations.

Why (FDA record): FDA inspection 740633 at Hospira, Inc. ended 2011-08-04, classified OAI with Form 483 observations for laboratory controls and investigation of discrepancies, 202 days before the shortage posting. FDA inspection 732886 at Hospira, Inc. ended 2011-06-17, classified OAI with 17 observations including control procedures and lack of a written stability program, 250 days before the shortage posting. FDA inspection 639034 at Hospira, Inc. ended 2010-01-19, classified OAI with 6 observations, 764 days before the shortage posting. A Warning Letter was issued to Hospira, Inc. on 2010-04-12, 681 days before the shortage posting.

Our position: Internal redistribution can stabilize Lakeside and General without new purchasing. Corvale East has sufficient stock to support both sites while retaining at least two weeks of supply.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 204 units of lidocaine hydrochloride products from Corvale East to Corvale Lakeside. Approval required: Pharmacy Director (transfer request).
2. Transfer 227 units of lidocaine hydrochloride products from Corvale East to Corvale General. Approval required: Pharmacy Director (transfer request).
3. Procure lidocaine hydrochloride 20 mg/mL from Medical Purchasing Solutions, LLC using the approved substitute NDC. Approval required: Pharmacist (Riley Brooks, PharmD approved 2026-08-12).

Not recommended: Purchasing from Avenacy, LLC or A-S Medication Solutions at this time; neither appears on the current FDA shortage list and supply reliability is unconfirmed.
